feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start = the first beams of the Booster, 26 May 1972. The PS page says the PS "usually accelerates either protons delivered by the Proton Synchrotron Booster or heavy ions from the Low Energy Ion Ring (LEIR)". Transfer energy to the PS: 2 GeV today, 1.4 GeV from 1999 to 2018 (see the era intervals).
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: Before the Booster received its first beams on 26 May 1972, protons were injected directly from Linac1 into the PS, where they were accelerated to 26 GeV.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.locator: end: home.cern, "All CERN accelerators now on the road to HiLumi", 31 August 2026
intervals.note: End = 31 August 2026, when "CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent." The 20 August 2026 accelerator report had scheduled the switch-off of all machines for 6.00 a.m. on Monday, 31 August.
intervals.quote: Before the Booster received its first beams on 26 May 1972, protons were injected directly from Linac1 into the PS, where they were accelerated to 26 GeV.

intervals.label: Linac2 era (50 MeV injection)
intervals.note: CERN's PSB page gives "1.4 GeV" for the whole of 1978 to 2018, but the Booster extracted 800 MeV at the start, 1 GeV later and only reached 1.4 GeV in 1999 (CERN Courier, see the "1.4 GeV extraction era" interval); the 1.4 GeV figure is therefore carried by that interval, not by this one.
intervals.quote: From 1978 until 2018, the Booster received protons from Linac2 at 50 MeV and accelerated them to 1.4 GeV for injection into the PS.

injection_energy.quote: From 1978 until 2018, the Booster received protons from Linac2 at 50 MeV and accelerated them to 1.4 GeV for injection into the PS.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (injector complex)
intervals.note: Start = 31 August 2026 (CERN news item of that date). End is a schedule value: "Following the long shutdown, CERN’s accelerator complex will gradually come back to life, beginning with Linac4, the PS Booster and ISOLDE at the start of 2028." (20 August 2026) and "The complex will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages." (31 August 2026).
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

intervals.label: Linac1 era (50 MeV injection)
intervals.note: Linac1 fed the Booster from its first beams until Linac2 replaced it in 1978 ("Linac2 started up in 1978, when it replaced Linac1.", CERN Linac2 page).
intervals.quote: The 50 MeV beam from Linac1 is distributed vertically and multiturn-injected into each ring.

injection_energy.quote: The 50 MeV beam from Linac1 is distributed vertically and multiturn-injected into each ring.

intervals.label: 800 MeV to 1 GeV extraction era
intervals.note: Extraction energy 800 MeV at the start (quote) and 1 GeV after "the PSB was promoted to a 1 GeV machine after minor hardware modifications"; ISOLDE was "relocated at the PSB in 1992" to use "the PSB's 1 GeV beam". No CERN source consulted dates the 800 MeV to 1 GeV step, so this interval records the range 0.8 to 1 GeV; the end is the 1999 upgrade to 1.4 GeV.
intervals.quote: On 26 May 1972, the PS Booster (PSB) accelerated its first protons to the design energy of 800 MeV.

beam_energy.note: Range 0.8 to 1 GeV, taken from the two figures in the quote (800 MeV at first beam, then 1 GeV after the promotion); the display shows its midpoint. The same article says ISOLDE moved to the Booster in 1992 to use its 1 GeV beam; the date of the step itself is not stated.
beam_energy.quote: On 26 May 1972, the PS Booster (PSB) accelerated its first protons to the design energy of 800 MeV. ... the PSB was promoted to a 1 GeV machine after minor hardware modifications

intervals.label: 1.4 GeV extraction era
intervals.locator: CERN Courier, "40 years of CERN's Proton Synchrotron"
intervals.note: Start from the 1999 CERN Courier article (the installation was "completed by early 2000" per the 2012 article); end from the PSB page ("From 1978 until 2018 ... 1.4 GeV"), after which the Linac4 / 2 GeV configuration began.
intervals.quote: In 1999 the harmful effects of space charge in the PS were reduced by raising the Booster energy to 1.4 GeV.

beam_energy.locator: CERN Courier, "40 years of CERN's Proton Synchrotron"
beam_energy.quote: In 1999 the harmful effects of space charge in the PS were reduced by raising the Booster energy to 1.4 GeV.

name: Proton Synchrotron Booster
notes: CONFLICT (era of the 1.4 GeV extraction energy): the CERN PSB page says the Booster "received protons from Linac2 at 50 MeV and accelerated them to 1.4 GeV" from 1978 until 2018; CERN Courier (1999) says the Booster energy was raised to 1.4 GeV in 1999, after 800 MeV (1972) and 1 GeV. The Courier dates are used for the 1.4 GeV interval; the PSB page is kept for the 50 MeV Linac2 injection.

beam_energy.quote: The ions are stripped of their two electrons during injection from Linac4 into the Proton Synchrotron Booster to leave only protons, which are accelerated to 2 GeV for injection into the Proton Synchrotron (PS).

injection_energy.note: Injection energy of the current configuration (Linac4, since 2020); 50 MeV with Linac1 and Linac2 (see the era intervals).
injection_energy.quote: receive beams of negative hydrogen ions (H-, consisting of a hydrogen atom with an additional electron) from the linear accelerator Linac4 at 160 MeV.

summary.plain: Four small accelerator rings stacked on top of each other that take particles from the linear accelerator and give them their first big push before the Proton Synchrotron. Adding the Booster in 1972 let CERN put more than a hundred times as many protons into the next machine.
summary.technical: Four superimposed synchrotron rings; receives 160 MeV H- from Linac4 (stripped to protons on injection) and accelerates to 2 GeV for the PS. From 1978 to 2018 it received 50 MeV protons from Linac2 and delivered 1.4 GeV.
